@graph.headline: Trading Journal: What to Track Beyond P&L (The Ledger, the Mirror, the Microscope)

acceptedAnswer.text: Three layers. The Ledger (what happened): date/time, instrument, direction, entry/stop/target/exit prices, position size, net P&L after Indian costs, result in R, and setup name from a fixed list. The Mirror (what you did): whether you followed your plan (yes/no), your execution score, planned vs actual R:R, the rule you broke and what it cost in rupees and R, and a chart screenshot. The Microscope (why it keeps happening): your emotional state, the session/time of day, and the valid setups you missed.

mainEntity.name: What should I track in a trading journal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Beyond the basics: your emotional state and whether you followed your trading plan on each trade. Practitioner consensus is blunt — most trading losses come from rule-breaking, not bad strategy — and tracking these two fields makes destructive patterns visible before they become account statements.

mainEntity.name: What is the most important thing to track in a trading journal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once a week: 30 minutes on the weekend, answering exactly three questions — which setup paid, which rule broke, and which hour bled. Once you accumulate 30+ trades, add a monthly review with setup-by-setup expectancy and the plan-followed vs not-followed comparison.

mainEntity.name: How often should I review my trading journal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as the starting point — free, flexible, and it handles the basics fine. It breaks down past roughly 5–10 trades a day, when manual entry and limited analytics become the bottleneck. The habit matters more than the tool; upgrade when volume forces it, not before.

mainEntity.name: Is a spreadsheet good enough for a trading journal?

acceptedAnswer.text: A trade's result expressed in units of its initial risk: risk ₹2,000 and make ₹4,000, that's +2R; lose the full risk, that's −1R. R-multiples normalize performance across position sizes and setups, so a 10-share trade and a 500-share trade can be compared on equal terms — which is exactly why the journal's result field is measured in R, not just rupees.

mainEntity.name: What is an R-multiple in trading?

acceptedAnswer.text: The plan layer — the part the Mirror owns: plan-followed yes/no, planned vs actual R:R, the rule you broke and what it cost in rupees and R, your execution score, and your emotional state before, during, and after the trade. Entry and exit prices record the trade; these fields record whether the trader showed up.
